Utah Code § 59-10-1042 (Social Security benefits credit; effective 1/1/2026 version)
header.notes: sha256 is of the canonical JSON body (JSON.stringify of the file without `header`). Values hand-transcribed; sha256 is of the canonical body. Rate: S.B. 60 (2026) cut the flat rate from 4.5% to 4.45% of Utah taxable income, with retrospective operation for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2026 (Tax Foundation's February 2026 table shows the superseded 4.5%). Utah taxable income starts from federal AGI with NO standard deduction or exemption deductions (standardDeduction 0). NOT EXPRESSIBLE IN THIS SCHEMA - taxpayer tax credit (Utah Code 59-10-1018): a nonrefundable credit of 6% x (federal standard deduction, or federal itemized deductions less state/local income tax, plus the Utah personal exemption per qualifying dependent - statutory $1,750 indexed, $2,111 for 2025), reduced by 1.3 cents per dollar of Utah taxable income above an indexed base (statutory $15,095 single / $22,643 head of household / $30,190 joint, indexed from 2020; 2025 amounts $18,213 single and MFS / $27,320 HOH / $36,426 joint; 2026 amounts not yet published). For a single 2026 filer the unreduced credit is 6% x $16,100 = $966 (Tax Foundation 2026: "$966 credit / $1,932 credit"). Social Security: federally taxable benefits are included in Utah income and offset by a nonrefundable credit (59-10-1042) equal to the tax rate (4.45%) x taxable benefits, reduced by 2.5 cents per dollar of modified AGI above $54,000 single, $90,000 joint and head of household, $45,000 married filing separately (statutory amounts, not indexed). Retirement income: no exclusion; an income-tested retirement credit exists only for those born on or before December 31, 1952 and cannot be combined with the Social Security credit (not modeled). No capital-gains exclusion. No local income taxes. Cross-checked against Tax Foundation, "State Individual Income Tax Rates and Brackets, 2026" (data as of Jan 1 2026, updated Feb 11 2026).
